text:
alex: Quick proposal TL;DR — tie control-plane locality routing fallback to tenant cost/accountability tags so we can make deterministic routing decisions when the per-tenant CP in-region is down. Thinking: preferred-region -> shared-fallback-region -> global-backup. Add cost-center header so downstream billing/alerts can attribute.
maria: can you sketch the contract you mean? curious how this differs from current cp fallback rules.
alex: current: simple latency-based fallback, no attribution. proposed contract: 1) tenant has preferred_region metadata; 2) control plane agent attempts preferred_region; 3) on failure, route to tenant-specific shared-fallback-region (configurable per-tenant); 4) as last resort, global-backup. Each routed request carries X-Redwood-Cost-Center and X-Redwood-Tenant-Region headers for billing/trace.
sam: i like explicitness. two quick Qs: how do we prevent noisy tenants from shifting large traffic to a cheaper region and blowing budgets? and how does this affect cert/DNS hell?
alex: good Q. mitigation ideas: a) rate-limits per fallback kind (canary/burst buckets) b) require a signed fallback-policy that includes max-fallback-qps and cost-center override c) prefer read-only or low-impact ops on fallback (no config changes unless authz allows)
ingrid: certs: if we handoff across regions we need mutual TLS proof between local CP and fallback CP. we should reuse the existing controlplane mTLS identity flow + include tenant-scoped SANs. DNS: use short TTLs for controlplane SRV records and have agent retry on NXDOMAIN->refresh flow.
patrick: small ops note: billing attribution requires collector to accept the headers and not trust client-supplied values blindly. we should stamp cost center at the first trusted hop (agent or relay) and log both stamped and observed values for auditing.
alex: exactly — agent stamps. example routing config snippet:
```
preferred_region: eu-west-1
fallback_regions:
  - eu-central-1
  - us-west-2
fallback_policy:
  max_qps: 20
  allowed_ops: [status,get-model-metadata]
  cost_center: org-foo:platform
```
sam: rollout plan idea: start with 5 tenants flagged as opt-in for fallback attribution; enable metrics: fallback_rate, fallback_cost_accum, fallback_latency_penalty. run for 2 weeks then iterate.
maria: for canary, we should expose a per-tenant dashboard in Console showing routing decisions and a per-route cost breakdown. ops should be able to flip policy to deny fallback instantly.
ingrid: noted: create playbook for cross-region failback and cert rotation (steps to re-sync SANs). add automated smoke test that exercises fallback and verifies header stamping and billing record emission.
patrick: one more: IAM — fallback CP must enforce the same tenant-scoped role bindings. We need to include tenant assertion token in handoff and have the fallback verify ephemeral assertion with CP identity service.
alex: agreed. next steps: i'll draft an RFC with example configs, rollout checklist, metric dashboards, and a short PoC agent change (stamp header + simple fallback policy). anyone want to be co-author?
maria: happy to help with the dashboard and rollout checklist.
sam: i'll take the PoC agent changes and unit tests.
ingrid: i'll write the cert/ops playbook and smoke tests.
devops-bot: Deploy-checklist reminder: create feature-flag `cp_locality_fallback_v1` and gate rollout. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks all — I'll start the RFC and ping later for reviews. :thumbsup:
